summary: The child listener is built to feel fear and suspense as the wolf waits in bed, knowing what the girl does not, and relief when the huntsman comes.

need-to-breathe.why: Nothing is built to affect the listener's breath.

hungry.why: The basket of cake and the wolf's three-day hunger are told, not built to make the listener hungry.

full.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

thirsty.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

gassy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-poop.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

need-to-pee.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

sleepy.why: A bedtime tale, but built to thrill before sleep, not to lull.

nauseous.why: Nothing is built to sicken the listener.

urge-to-sneeze.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

urge-to-cough.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

dizzy.why: Nothing is built to produce vertigo.

fatigued.why: The listener is not made to feel exertion.

pain.why: The wolf's belly cut open and sewn with stones gives a small wince, softened by the fairy-tale telling.

disgusted.why: Being swallowed whole, the hairy wolf in a nightcap, and the slit belly are built for a child's delighted shudder.

itchy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

tickled.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

over-stimulated.why: Nothing is built to overwhelm the senses.

too-hot-too-cold.why: Nothing is built to make the listener feel heat or cold.

afraid.why: The wolf in grandmother's bed, the mounting questions, and the teeth are built to frighten a child, the tale's chief effect.

anxious.why: From the moment the girl tells the wolf where she is going, the listener dreads what the listener knows is coming.

panic.why: The pounce is over in a sentence; the listener gasps rather than panics.

sensory-pleasures.why: The flowers and sunshine of the wood are a brief pleasure before the trap.

aesthetic-pleasures.why: The ritual exchange, what big ears you have, is built as a formula the listener savors and can chant along with.

piquancy.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

fun-excitement.why: The chant and the pounce, and in Grimm the rescue and the second wolf's drowning, are built as a child's thrilling game.

orgasm.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

love-romantic.why: Perrault's moral about seducers is for adults; the tale does not build romantic feeling.

love-family.why: The errand to a sick grandmother is built to engage the child's family feeling.

grief.why: Perrault's ending can grieve a child briefly; Grimm restores everyone.

missing-someone.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

aroused-sexually.why: Nothing is built to arouse the listener; the seduction reading is a moral, not an effect.

liking-as-a-friend.why: The listener is built to like the trusting girl and to see through the wolf's false friendliness.

empathy.why: The child listener is built to stand in the girl's place at the bedside, question by question.

compassion.why: The sick grandmother and the trusting girl are built to produce the child's pity.

grateful.why: Nothing is built to make the listener grateful.

pleasure-from-helping.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

trustful-distrustful.why: The listener knows the wolf is a wolf and that the voice in bed is his while the girl trusts him; the tale runs on this irony.

depressed.why: Nothing is built to lower the listener's mood.

angry.why: The wolf's trick may anger a child, but the tale builds fear more than anger.

envious.why: Nothing is built to produce envy.

jealous-romantic-sexual.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

jealous-friendship.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

hatred.why: The wolf is built as the villain a child may hate, briefly.

contempt.why: Nothing is built to produce scorn.

resentment.why: Nothing is built to produce a sense of violated rules, except the girl's own straying.

proud.why: Nothing is built to make the listener proud.

amused.why: The wolf in a nightcap and the chanted questions are built for comedy alongside the fright.

sense-of-belonging.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

lonely.why: The grandmother alone in the wood gives a faint sense of isolation.

judgy-moral-sense.why: Perrault's moral and Grimm's lesson about leaving the path are built to make the child judge the girl's mistake and the wolf's crime.

admiration.why: The huntsman's rescue is built for a small admiration.

embarrassed.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

shame.why: Nothing is built to shame the listener.

guilt.why: The Grimm girl's resolve is meant to prompt a child to think of its own disobedience, faintly.

sad.why: Perrault's ending leaves a child sad; Grimm does not.

happy.why: Grimm's ending, with all three safe and the cake eaten, is built to leave a child content.

joyful-euphoric.why: The girl springing from the wolf's belly is built as a burst of relief and joy.

effort.why: A few pages; nothing demands persistence.

focused-in-flow.why: The tale is built to hold a child rapt from the wood to the teeth.

impatient.why: The question-by-question delay at the bedside is built to make the listener strain toward the pounce.

curious.why: The listener wants to know how the girl will discover the wolf and what happens when she does.

surprised.why: For a first-time child the teeth and the gulp are built to startle, and the huntsman's rescue to astonish.

awe.why: Nothing is built to produce awe.

skeptical-doubtful.why: The listener doubts the grandmother in the bed before the girl does, doubt the tale invites with each big feature.

feeling-of-knowing.why: Nothing is built to make a clue almost land.

frustrated.why: The girl's slowness to see the wolf is built to frustrate the listener who sees him plainly.

uncertain-certain.why: The listener is certain of the wolf and uncertain only whether the girl will be saved.

understanding.why: The tale is built so the child understands its lesson, do not talk to wolves, by the end.

inspired.why: Nothing is built to give the listener a flash of insight.

satisfied.why: Grimm's version closes with the wolf dead and the girl wiser, a tidy satisfaction; Perrault's refuses it.

foreboding.why: The listener knows the wolf is a wolf from his first word, so every step toward the cottage is built as dread.

nostalgia.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

anticipation-suspense.why: The wolf in the bed and the chant of questions are built as pure suspense toward the pounce.

hope.why: The listener hopes the girl will notice in time, and in Grimm that the huntsman will come.

schadenfreude.why: The wolf dying of his stones and the second wolf drowning are built to be enjoyed.

elevation.why: The huntsman's rescue offers a small lift.

infatuation.why: Nothing is built to produce this.

rage.why: Nothing is built to produce rage.
